g.text: user: User (FK, UK) ' NOT NULL - every storefront has an owner
*catalog_vendor: CatalogVendor (FK, PK) ' 1:1 extension, not a 2nd user link
unit: UnitOfMeasure (FK) ' must be a member of comparison_group's allowed units
stock_quantity: int ' default 0 - maintained by the inventory trigger
order: Order (FK, null) ' set when the movement came from a sale
user: User (FK, null) ' NULL only for anonymous WALK_IN sales
customer_label: str (null) ' walk-in name, when there is no User row
vendor: CatalogVendor (FK) ' NOT NULL - one order = one vendor
unit_price: decimal ' price snapshot at order time
provider: str ' GCASH | MAYA | BANK | CARD | CASH
provider: str ' GRABEXPRESS | LALAMOVE | MAXIM | LOCAL
receipt_attempt: int ' default 1; increments on reprint
One Order holds products from ONE vendor only (vendor NOT NULL).
Multi-vendor checkout = one Order per vendor
(split in OrderListCreateView.post), each with its own Transaction,
its own Payment and - for delivery - its own DeliveryBooking.
WALK_IN sales (vendor POS) are Orders with user = NULL and
fulfillment_type = WALK_IN, so anonymous buyers need no User row.
raw card numbers or banking passwords.
CASH payments are recorded here too (provider = 'CASH',
provider_reference = the receipt serial), so all money received
One-to-one with Transaction. Created only for
DELIVERY fulfillment after payment is verified.
Pickup orders have no delivery booking.
are written by the vendor's out-for-delivery / delivered actions.
Vendor POS record linked to an Order.
receipt_attempt increments on every reprint, so a reprinted
receipt keeps the same serial and stays auditable.
Transaction is a linked commercial record (reference_no +
transaction_type), NOT the order itself. Order is the order entity.
and POS_WALKIN - this is what makes "show me all reservations"
Transaction carries NO status of its own. Lifecycle lives once, on
Order.status; settlement lives once, on Payment.status. Storing a
third copy here would be a second authority for the same fact with
nothing keeping the two in step.
